notes: Numbers: both attempts' headline numbers are correct and agree with each other and with my reruns (full +4.25 pp, t interval +3.36..+5.14; clean 0.00, -0.89..+0.89; dup subset +17.00, +13.06..+20.94; 40 exact duplicates; mechanism counts 243/157 identical in both). B/test_clean.csv is byte-identical to A's. Errors not covered by assertions: (1) B says the nearest clean test ticket is 'cách hơn 0,29' from train; the actual minimum is 0.394 (A reports 0.394 correctly). B's statement is literally true but the figure is not produced by run_experiment.py, so it is untraceable. (2) B's per-seed table shows seed 3 full diff +4,37 and clean -0,84 where exact values are +4.375 and -0.833: artefacts of differencing 4-decimal rounded accuracies; A computes from hit counts. A in turn prints 89/160 as 55,62 where experiment.py prints 0.5563. All cosmetic. (3) A's runs.jsonl 'command' is a template covering three invocations, and 'python' rather than 'python3'; not a copy-pasteable command. (4) A's plan cites an unpaired MDE of ~17 pp for n=120, which is far more pessimistic than the paired S1 interval of about +/-2 pp it later reports; the plan says pairing needs fewer rows but the 17 pp figure is of little use. Quality differences the assertions do not separate: B went beyond A in substance: k sweep (1,3,5,7,9,15) showing the same pattern at every k, tie-break analysis (147/1200 uniform ties on clean), a ticket-level bootstrap on the full set as well, and the point that an exact-match lookup would be clearer if production does see repeated tickets. A deliberately refused any variant beyond the two arms and so cannot say whether the null on clean data holds at other k. However B's extras are unplanned and unlabelled as exploratory, and its recommendation 3 (try k = 15, 52.00% -> 56.67%) is selected on the test set, though B caveats it. B's report is much shorter and directly readable by a returning owner; A's is long, mixes English template headings with Vietnamese, and carries process vocabulary (G1-G4, H1/H2, S1) the owner must decode, but it gives full auditability: frozen plan, lock, timestamped log, decisions table, self-review with findings, hit counts per run. A also explicitly states the condition under which its own framing is wrong (production tickets that can duplicate train tickets); B makes the same point in recommendation 2. A is careful to call the clean result 'inconclusive, not equal'; B says 'hai phương pháp bằng nhau' and 'đổi sang không gây hại về accuracy', which is stronger than a +/-2 pp ticket-level interval supports. Timestamps of files in A/ and B/ are copy times (all 08:40:09), so plan-freeze evidence rests on .plan.lock frozen_at vs run 'date' fields, both written by A's own tooling.
